scenario_parameters.agent_goal: Meet your monthly target customer satisfaction rate of 70% by responding to consumer queries about their housing loans. Each interaction rated '<Satisfied>' or above ADDS to your satisfaction rate. Each interaction rated '<Dissatisfied>' or below SUBTRACTS from your satisfaction rate.

dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hello! Thank you for responding. I'm inquiring about the status of my housing loan application that I submitted recently. Could you please tell me if it's still pending or if there's been a decision made on it?
dialogue.agent: I've located your application. According to our records, the action taken on your housing loan application was that it was denied. The principal reason for the denial was insufficient cash for down payment and closing costs. Is there anything specific you'd like to know about the application or the denial reasons?

dialogue.user: I'm sorry to hear that my application was denied. Insufficient cash for down payment and closing costs makes sense, I guess I was a bit worried about that. Can you tell me what my interest rate would have been if my application had been approved? And were there any other significant issues with my application that contributed to the denial, or was it mainly the down payment and closing costs?
dialogue.agent: The interest rate information is not available in the record, as the application was denied. Regarding other significant issues, the record shows that the debt-to-income ratio was 46%, but there's no indication that this was a factor in the denial. The denial reason listed is only "Insufficient cash (downpayment, closing costs)". There are no other denial reasons recorded.

dialogue.user: So, the debt-to-income ratio was high, but it wasn't a factor in the denial. That's a bit reassuring, I suppose. Can you tell me what my loan term would have been if my application had been approved? And has my loan been transferred or sold to another institution, even though it was denied?
dialogue.agent: According to the record, the loan term would have been 300 months. As for the second question, since your application was denied, the loan was not sold or transferred to another institution. The "Purchaser Type" field in the record is not applicable in this case, as it only applies to loans that were originated and then sold.

dialogue.user: The loan term of 300 months makes sense, that's what I was expecting. Okay, so since the loan wasn't sold or transferred, that means I'm not responsible for repaying a loan that wasn't even approved. That clears things up. Can you tell me if there were any high-cost or negative amortization flags on my loan, even though it was denied? And finally, what type of loan product was I approved for... wait, I mean, what type of loan product was my application for?
dialogue.agent: The record does not show any high-cost mortgage classification under HOEPA, and there's no negative amortization feature associated with your loan. As for the loan product type, your application was for a Conventional loan, specifically a Conventional:First Lien loan product, for the purpose of a home purchase.

dialogue.user: So, my application was for a Conventional loan for a home purchase, and it didn't have any high-cost or negative amortization features, even though it was denied. That helps me understand the situation better. I think I've got all the information I need. I'm going to rate this interaction as <Satisfied>. I'm satisfied because you were able to provide clear and direct answers to all my questions, and you helped me understand the denial reason and the details of my application. Your responses were helpful and professional.
